rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes monotonic tensile tests on polycrystalline samples, whereas the paper used compression of [1̄23]-oriented single crystals to measure CRSS; the intervention type (tensile vs. compression) and sample form (polycrystal vs. single crystal) differ fundamentally.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature, constant-strain-rate tensile testing, while the paper's main regime spans 9–1373 K compression at 1e-4 s^-1 with strain-rate jumps; only the room-temperature point overlaps, missing the cryogenic and high-temperature conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes stacking fault energy variations and strain hardening differences, whereas the paper's mechanisms are solid-solution strengthening via MSAD, inertial dulling, and Cottrell-type PL pinning; these are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower ductility and altered strain hardening in fewer-component alloys, while the paper measures CRSS changes with temperature and composition, finding increased strength with Cr and PL effects with Mn/Fe; the predicted property and direction do not match.
